newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi leader departs for sanctions summit.
newsitem.headline: Burundi leader departs for sanctions summit.

text.p: Burundi leader Major Pierre Buyoya left on Tuesday for the first regional meeting in Tanzania since neighbouring countries imposed an economic embargo to force him to restore democracy.

Witnesses said Buyoya, who overthrew civilian Hutu president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya last year, left on his presidential jet for a heads of state summit on Wednesday in the northern Tanzanian city of Arusha.

The summit will decide whether to tighten or lift transport and economic sanctions imposed last July 31 to force Buyoya into talks with Hutu rebels. It is the first time Buyoya will be at a regional meeting since the embargo was imposed.
A United Nations study of the sanctions released this week found no hard evidence they had succeeded in their political aims while smuggling was weakening their impact.
Initial findings issued on Tuesday by the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs suggested Burundi sanctions should be retargetted to protect the vulnerable and more items exempted for aid agencies.
